documents.title: Upper Endoscopy Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology - endoscopy unit
Procedure date: 02/10/2026
Patient: Abigail Paquette, DOB 07/27/1980
Procedure: esophagogastroduodenoscopy with cold forceps biopsy
Indication: dysphagia to solids and liquids; esophagram with corkscrew contractions.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care, propofol per anesthesia record.
Allergies: NKDA.

Findings:
- Esophagus: normal caliber and mucosa throughout. No rings, furrows, exudate, stricture or mass. Z-line regular. Biopsies taken from the distal and the proximal/mid esophagus to exclude eosinophilic esophagitis.
- Stomach: normal mucosa; retroflexion normal, no hiatal hernia.
- Duodenum: normal through the second portion.
The scope traversed the GE junction without resistance.

Impression: normal upper endoscopy; no structural cause for dysphagia. Pathology pending.
Recommendations: follow up in GI clinic 03/03/2026 as scheduled. Resume regular diet today.
No complications. Discharged home with an escort.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Clinic Note
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology group
Visit date: 03/03/2026
Patient: Abigail Paquette, 45 y/o F
Referring: primary care physician

Reason for visit: return visit after EGD; dysphagia.

HPI: Ms. Paquette comes back to clinic roughly a year after ENT first saw her for this. Over the past six months she has had on-and-off trouble getting both solids and liquids down, episodes of undigested food coming back up, and now and then pain behind the sternum. She ties many episodes to emotionally stressful stretches at work. No weight loss, no vomiting, no hematemesis or melena.

Problem list: esophageal dysmotility.
Medications: none.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family history: hypothyroidism in her mother, hypertension in her father.
Social: never smoker, 1-2 alcoholic drinks weekly, works as a corporate project manager.

Exam: normal. Well appearing, abdomen soft and nontender, no lymphadenopathy.

Data reviewed:
- Barium esophagram 10/07/2025: intermittent corkscrew-type contractions of the esophagus, no structural lesion.
- EGD 02/10/2026: no structural abnormality. Biopsies benign without eosinophilia.

Assessment: esophageal dysmotility. The corkscrew pattern with a structurally normal esophagus most suggests a spastic disorder such as distal esophageal spasm; achalasia needs to be excluded before treatment is chosen.

Plan:
1. High-resolution esophageal manometry - ordered.
2. Avoid very hot and very cold drinks, eat slowly with smaller bites, stay upright for a while after meals.
3. No medication for now; will decide after manometry.
4. Telehealth follow-up after the study.

Gastroenterology

reports.text: Solid-state high-resolution manometry, Chicago Classification v4.0 protocol. Upper esophageal sphincter: normal resting pressure and relaxation. EGJ: median IRP 9 mmHg (normal). Esophageal body, 10 supine wet swallows: 4 premature (distal latency under 4.5 s), 6 normal peristalsis; no failed or hypercontractile swallows. Upright and multiple rapid swallows concordant.
reports.conclusion: Distal esophageal spasm (Chicago Classification v4.0). Normal EGJ relaxation; no achalasia.

documents.title: High-Resolution Esophageal Manometry
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology - motility laboratory
Study date: 04/08/2026
Patient: Abigail Paquette, DOB 07/27/1980
Indication: dysphagia; esophagram with corkscrew contractions; normal EGD.

Protocol: solid-state high-resolution catheter placed transnasally without difficulty. Supine 10 water swallows, followed by upright swallows and multiple rapid swallows per Chicago Classification v4.0. Patient tolerated well.

Upper esophageal sphincter: normal resting pressure and relaxation.
Esophagogastric junction: median integrated relaxation pressure 9 mmHg (normal).
Esophageal body (supine): 10 wet swallows evaluated. 4 of 10 premature (distal latency less than 4.5 seconds). The remaining 6 showed normal peristalsis. No failed and no hypercontractile swallows.
Upright and provocative maneuvers: consistent with the supine findings.

Interpretation: normal EGJ relaxation with premature contractions in 40% of swallows. Meets criteria for distal esophageal spasm (Chicago Classification v4.0). No evidence of achalasia.

Motility laboratory, gastroenterology

documents.title: Gastroenterology Telehealth Follow-up
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology group - video visit 04/21/2026
Patient: Abigail Paquette

Reviewed her manometry with her: normal sphincter relaxation and premature contractions on 4 of 10 swallows, which classifies her esophageal dysmotility as distal esophageal spasm. Achalasia excluded. This matches the corkscrew esophagram and her symptom triggers.

We talked through management. Episodes remain intermittent. Because they are intermittent and she does well between them, she would like to keep to the measures already in place rather than start a medication. Reasonable. If episodes become more frequent or harder to tolerate, a trial of a calcium channel blocker is the next step, and we would revisit other options after that.

Plan: continue avoiding temperature extremes in drinks, small bites, eating slowly, upright after meals. No medications started. Return to GI clinic in about six months, sooner as needed. Medications: none. Allergies: NKDA.

Gastroenterology
